from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3357FF"), FadeIn(k_vec))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Dot product measures similarity between two vectors.",
            "Query multiplied by Key gives raw attention scores.",
            "High scores mean more focus on that word.",
            "'It' pays attention to 'cat' over 'mat'.",
            "This creates our attention heatmap."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism: Calculating Attention Scores", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        formula = MathTex(r"\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        highlight = MathTex(r"\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}", color="#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(highlight, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(highlight))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        score_viz = Text("Scores", color="#33FF57").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(score_viz, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(highlight, score_viz))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        weight_viz = Text("Weighted Values", color="#3357FF").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(weight_viz, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(weight_viz))
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#3357FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        final_block = Rectangle(color="#CCCCCC", width=4, height=1.5)
        label = Text("Attention Heatmap", color="#CCCCCC").scale(0.6)
        group = VGroup(final_block, label)
        self.place_in_area(group, 'E2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(final_block), Write(label))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#CCCCCC"))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Softmax and Weighting", [
            "Scores can be large and unmanageable.",
            "Softmax maps scores to a zero-one range.",
            "Attention becomes a probability distribution.",
            "The spotlight highlights relevant words clearly.",
            "Weights sum up to one perfectly."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Scores [2, 1, -1]
        scores = VGroup(*[MathTex(s, color=WHITE) for s in ["2", "1", "-1"]])
        scores.arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(scores, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(scores))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition to Softmax [0.67, 0.24, 0.09]
        probs = VGroup(*[MathTex(s, color="#FF5733") for s in ["0.67", "0.24", "0.09"]])
        probs.arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(probs, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Transform(scores, probs))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Represent distribution
        dist_label = Text("Attention Weights", font_size=20, color="#33FF57")
        self.place_at_grid(dist_label, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(dist_label))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Spotlight (placeholder as primitive)
        spotlight = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#33FF57", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(spotlight, 'E4', scale_factor=1.5)

        self.play(spotlight.animate.shift(LEFT*1.5))
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "One attention head is rarely enough.",
            "Parallel heads capture different types of relationships.",
            "One head tracks grammar, another tracks tone.",
            "Combining heads provides a complete understanding.",
            "Multi-head attention mimics human cognition."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Whole Picture", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create heads
        head_colors = ["#FF5733", "#33FF57", "#3357FF", "#FFFF33"]
        heads = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=1.5, color=c) for c in head_colors])
        head_labels = VGroup(*[Text(f"Head {i+1}", font_size=16) for i in range(4)])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Split screen into four smaller regions
        grid_pos = ["B2", "B5", "E2", "E5"]
        for i, pos in enumerate(grid_pos):
            self.place_at_grid(heads[i], pos, scale_factor=0.4)
            self.place_at_grid(head_labels[i], pos, scale_factor=1.0)
            head_labels[i].next_to(heads[i], DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(heads), Write(head_labels))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Parallel heads performing attention
        self.play(*[Indicate(heads[i]) for i in range(4)])
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Head 1 (grammar), Head 2 (tone)
        self.play(
            heads[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"),
            heads[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57")
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Concatenation
        concat_bar = Rectangle(height=0.5, width=4, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(concat_bar, "C4", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(concat_bar))
        self.play(FadeIn(concat_bar))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Final output
        output_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color="#CCCCCC")
        self.place_at_grid(output_vec, "D4", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(GrowArrow(output_vec))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
outline.target_audience: University students with basic programming/math background

sections.title: The Problem: Context Blindness
sections.content: Introduce the challenge of reading a long sentence where words depend on previous words (Recurrent Neural Networks). Show how old methods lose context over long distances.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The bank of the river is muddy,' the word 'bank' is ambiguous. A simple model forgets 'river' by the time it reaches 'bank'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Query, Key, and Value (QKV)
sections.content: Explain the retrieval system analogy. Query (what I want), Key (what I offer), Value (the actual information). Use a graphical 'Library Catalog' analogy.
sections.example: Think of a student (Query) searching for a book in a library. The book spine label is the 'Key', and the content inside the book is the 'Value'.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Calculating Attention Scores
sections.content: Visualizing the Dot Product. Explain that we multiply the Query by the Key to find how much 'attention' word A should pay to word B. Use a heatmap animation.
sections.example: In 'The cat sat on the mat because it was tired,' calculate the attention scores: 'it' has a high dot-product match with 'cat' (the subject) vs. 'mat' (the object).

sections.title: Softmax and Weighting
sections.content: Convert raw scores into probabilities (0-1 range) using Softmax. This ensures the model 'distributes' attention across all words intelligently.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Spotlight' beam moving across words. 'it' puts 80% of its spotlight on 'cat' and 20% on 'mat' to resolve ambiguity.

sections.title: Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Whole Picture
sections.content: Explain that one 'head' isn't enough. We run multiple attention layers in parallel to capture different types of relationships (e.g., grammatical vs. semantic).
sections.example: Like having one editor check for grammar (Head 1) while another checks for the emotional tone of the story (Head 2), combining results for a complete understanding.
